Also figurative online: 没营养的话题 is a vacuous topic, 有营养 means worth reading or watching.
In Journey to the West, Sun Wukong is often called 行者 or 孙行者 as Tang Sanzang's disciple.
A formal or mock-formal "I", common in notices, statements and online posts: 本人郑重声明 ("I hereby solemnly declare").

gloss: oneself; yourself; himself; herself; the person concerned
note: On forms and at service counters, the person in question acting in person: 须本人到场办理 ("must be handled in person").

gloss: outside (also pr. [wai4 mian5] for this sense)
note: In speech, 他在外面有人 means he has a lover outside his marriage. 在外面吃 means eating out.
Mostly in 桃花运 ("luck in love"), a term from fortune-telling. 烂桃花 are unwanted or troublesome romances.
Usually someone in their early to mid teens, younger than a 青年. Also in 少年犯 ("juvenile offender") and 少年宫, a children's activity centre.
Formal; news reports use it for officials and guests attending meetings and ceremonies. Friends 参加 a party rather than 出席 it.
Often a career goal: 你的理想是什么？ asks children what they want to be when they grow up.
不太理想 is a soft way of saying results were poor: 考试成绩不太理想.
In slogans and ads, 有温度 means humane or caring: 有温度的服务 ("service with a human touch").
A core word in official language: 民族团结 ("ethnic unity") and 安定团结 ("stability and unity") are fixed slogans.
Formally chosen by the provincial people's congress, and ranks below the provincial Party secretary.

gloss: (fig.) to proceed from (a particular standpoint or basis)
note: A staple of official writing: 从实际出发 ("proceed from actual conditions"), 从群众利益出发.
Marks what is private or unofficial as opposed to state-run: 民间资本 ("private capital"), 民间借贷 ("informal lending").
Also means giving approval: 领导点头了 ("the boss signed off"). 点头之交 is a nodding acquaintance.
In PRC political language, remaking people's thinking: 思想改造 ("thought reform") and 劳动改造 ("reform through labour"), shortened to 劳改.
Also short for 中国移动, China Mobile, the largest mobile carrier: 移动卡 is a China Mobile SIM. 移动支付 is paying by phone.
The lowest level of city government, below the district. 街道办 handles local paperwork and services, with 居委会 working under its guidance.
Usually in 一口咬定, to insist on a claim and refuse to budge, and 一口否认, to deny outright.
Common in speech: 回头见 ("see you later"), 回头再说 ("let's deal with it later"), which can also mean putting something off for good.
Official language extends it to anyone praised as fighting for a cause: 白衣战士 for medical workers, 抗疫战士 during the pandemic.
In China, attached to areas with large ethnic minority populations: 自治区, 自治州 and 自治县, such as the Tibet Autonomous Region.
Zones set up by governments since the 1980s to draw investment with tax breaks and cheap land, often on a city's edge: 经济技术开发区.
A rung in China's administrative ladder. A 县级市 is a city ranked as a county, below prefecture-level cities.
Used in official and technical contexts. At markets and in everyday talk weights are given in 斤, half a 公斤.
Describes a vast mass on the move, such as a crowd, army or river: 浩浩荡荡的队伍 ("a huge procession streaming along").
A core principle in PRC official language, as in 独立自主的和平外交政策, the "independent foreign policy of peace".

gloss: (of one's name, reputation etc) to be immortalized (idiom)
note: Formal praise for historical figures, often set against its opposite 遗臭万年, "to leave a name that stinks for ten thousand years".

gloss: (idiom) to gnash one's teeth; to fume with rage
note: Usually expresses bitter hatred rather than passing anger: 恨得咬牙切齿 ("to hate someone with clenched teeth").

gloss: not a word or movement (idiom); remaining calm and collected
note: Often describes someone acting while hiding their intentions: 不动声色地观察 means watching closely without giving anything away.

gloss: (idiom) military title said to have existed in the Han dynasty, allegedly granted to officials tasked with retrieving gold from tombs to fund military campaigns; (in popular fiction) tomb raider
note: Best known today from the tomb-raiding novel series 鬼吹灯 (Ghost Blows Out the Light), which made it a popular nickname for grave robbers.

gloss: to be the master of one's own affairs
note: A key phrase of PRC political language: 人民当家作主 ("the people are masters of the country") describes the official basis of the state.
Strongly linked to Mao's slogan 全心全意为人民服务, "serve the people wholeheartedly", still the stated purpose of the Communist Party.
Mostly said of places and their natural conditions: 得天独厚的地理位置. A stock phrase in tourism and investment promotion.
Praise for a distinctive style or approach, not a sign of being a loner: 他的画风独树一帜 ("his painting style is one of a kind").

gloss: to show off one's military strength (idiom); to strut around
note: Always disapproving: showing off power to intimidate others, said of bullies, petty officials or an occupying army.

gloss: to do sth when least expected (idiom); to catch sb off guard
note: From the Art of War (孙子兵法): 攻其无备，出其不意, "attack where they are unprepared, appear where they do not expect".
Mostly heard as a good wish before an exam, contest or new venture: 祝你马到成功！ ("wishing you swift success!").

gloss: not to accept as correct (idiom); to object
note: Means disagreeing or disapproving, and is often misused for 不以为意, "not taking something seriously".

gloss: lit. to govern from behind the curtain
note: Best known from Empress Dowager Cixi, who ruled for boy emperors from behind a screen. Now also used for anyone pulling strings behind a nominal leader.
A stock phrase of police reports and official rhetoric, usually as the target of a crackdown: 打击犯罪分子的嚣张气焰.

gloss: (idiom) to experience the joy of being newly married
note: From the Book of Songs (诗经), where the line 宴尔新昏 is a rejected wife's lament about her husband's new bride. Now simply a happy phrase for newlyweds.

gloss: illustrious hero, spirit of the place (idiom); a place derives reflected glory from an illustrious son
note: From Wang Bo's 滕王阁序. Now a stock compliment for a region in speeches and local promotion: 我们这里人杰地灵.
Almost always disapproving: acting without any restraint, as with officials or the powerful who 为所欲为.
Neutral, used for both good and bad things: 新产品层出不穷 and 骗局层出不穷 ("scams keep cropping up") are both common.

gloss: (fig.) to die horribly; to sacrifice one's life
note: Mostly heard in vows of devotion: 粉身碎骨也在所不辞, "would not shrink even from death".
First used by the Han writer Dongfang Shuo about the danger of advising a ruler. Now said of a plan that is far harder than it sounds.
Often mocking: 一本正经地胡说八道 ("talking nonsense with a straight face") is a common online phrase for confident bluffing.
Not always critical: it can simply mean a leader giving orders, but often mocks someone who orders others about and does no work.

gloss: lit. heart untroubled, spirit pleased (idiom); carefree and relaxed
note: Usually describes the effect of scenery, fresh air or a view from a height. Well known from Fan Zhongyan's essay 岳阳楼记, memorized in school.
From the Shiji story of Mao Sui, who likened talent to an awl in a bag whose point pokes through. Now common for winners of contests and selections.

gloss: in the right and self-confident (idiom); bold and confident with justice on one's side
note: Often ironic, for someone in the wrong acting fully confident: 迟到了还理直气壮 ("late, and acting as if in the right").
A stock phrase of reports and official documents: 行之有效的措施 ("effective measures"). Rare in casual speech.

gloss: to keep on saying (idiom); to repeat over and over again
note: Usually implies the words are not matched by deeds: 他口口声声说爱你 casts doubt on whether he does.

gloss: to threaten the east and strike to the west (idiom)
note: One of the Thirty-Six Stratagems (三十六计). Also used of feints in sport and business.
A stock phrase of official statements: 别有用心的人 labels critics or agitators as acting from hidden, hostile motives.

gloss: to arise at an opportune time
note: Now usually said of products, services or businesses that appear because demand calls for them: 外卖平台应运而生.

gloss: (idiom) to replace; to supersede; to take its (or her etc) place
note: From the Shiji: the young Xiang Yu, seeing the First Emperor's procession, said 彼可取而代也. Now used for any replacement.

gloss: lit. shocks the eye, astonishes the heart (idiom); shocking
note: Often used of figures and reports, not only sights: 数据触目惊心 means the numbers are alarming. Common in news on disasters and corruption.

gloss: (idiom) all under heaven; in the whole world; throughout the world

note: From the Shiji story of Mao Sui, who likened talent to an awl in a bag whose point pokes through. Now common for winners of contests and selections.
